messages:
maria: Noticing sustained egress queueing on west-2b GPU nodes. mlx5 tx_qdrop counters climbing, p95 TCP retransmit up ~20%. Early signs point to NIC egress saturation rather than disk.
jon: Copy. Any correlation with a recent model rollout or large-batch jobs? kubelet logs show some pod eviction warnings on affected nodes.
maria: No recent model push to that zone. Top talkers are inference endpoints and a few bulk-embeddings jobs. ifstat shows egress near line rate on a subset of hosts.
tess: Prioritize pod-level actions: cordon the worst nodes, drain batch/embeddings first, keep pinned low-latency routes on healthy hosts. We can't afford inference timeouts.
kai: Routing plan: shift ~60% of traffic off west-2b into west-2a warm pool, leaving ~40% to avoid cold-start storms. I'll update smart-router weight rules and start a staged spill.
akshay: Heads-up on cost: moving 60% will spin more on-demand in west-2a. Rough estimate 180-240 GPU-hours incremental for next 12h. Finance FYI.
maria: Agreed we accept cost for now. Also let's temporarily drop batch aggregation windows and cap parallel connections per process to lower burst egress.
kai: Drain commands I'm running now (batch first):
```
kubectl get nodes -l zone=west-2b,pool=gpu-pocket -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl cordon
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l zone=west-2b,pool=gpu-pocket -o name); do kubectl drain ${n} --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --pod-selector='role=batch' --grace-period=60 && sleep 20; done
```
Will leave latency-critical pods alone.
jon: I'll reduce max_context_tokens and throttle heavy model loads for non-prod routes. Also will watch kubelet evictions and restart loops.
infra-bot: autoscaler: detected spill to west-2a; provisioning 12 g5-equivalents (mix spot/on-demand) to warm-pool.
tess: No new deploys in west-2b until we get stable metrics. Hold canaries and feature flags there.
deploy-bot: deployment/embeddings-worker paused in west-2b as precaution.
maria: Ops checklist: 1) confirm if host-level qdisc defaults (fq_codel) need tuning 2) check ethtool -S for NIC errors 3) search logs for tcp_retransmit and conntrack drops.
kai: Routing change in 30s: will move to west-2a:60%, west-2b:40% over 3 steps. Observability will be on a 1-min cadence.
jon: Noting conntrack table on a few hosts hit 80% — I'll increase the conntrack max on nodes showing thrashing and drain if it keeps climbing.
akshay: If west-2a saturates, fallback plan is west-1c cross-region spill (latency +90ms, much higher egress cost). Call it only if node provision fails.
maria: Monitoring dash links: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/nic-egress?var-zone=west-2b and logs query: https://logs.redwood/prod/_search?q=tx_qdrop+zone:west-2b
kai: Routing policy applied step1: west-2a:40 / west-2b:60. Observing for 2 minutes before next step.
jon: After step1 p95 retransmit -> 12% (down from 20%). Conntrack still a hotspot on two nodes; increasing net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max temporarily.
tess: Good. Post-incident: 1) add synthetic egress saturation test for GPU pockets 2) document per-host qdisc & conntrack tuning 3) evaluate whether ML batch jobs should be rate-limited by controller.
infra-bot: routing-policy update applied: west-2a:60%, west-2b:40%. Warm-pool scale triggered.
maria: Metrics improving: p95 retransmit ~8%, tx_qdrop trend flattening. Continue drains until qdrops < 1% sustained.
kai: I'll finish draining remaining batch nodes and leave a small steady-state of inference capacity in west-2b to avoid full cold-cache miss.
akshay: Will track cost delta and open a quick MBR note. If we end up using west-1c will escalate to leadership for approval.
jon: Keeping watch on pod restarts; no OOMs observed. If evictions resume, we escalate to hardware/host oncall.
tess: Filing follow-ups in #postmortems: include runbook tweaks for NIC qdisc tuning, conntrack sizing, and router weight automation for spill scenarios.
maria: Thanks team. If anything degrades we escalate to oncall-lead. For now routing spill and drains look good :thumbsup:
